summary_html: Court issues a **protective or restraining order** to prevent contact, remove abuser, or ensure safety without removing the child. Federal law leaves implementation to states but funds protection efforts through CAPTA and IV-B.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — authorizes protective interventions and state plan requirements  
- **SSA Title IV-B** — permits funding for protective services and court interventions

primary_citations.citation_text: South Dakota - S.D. Codified Laws Chapter 26-8A (Protection of Children from Abuse or Neglect – mandatory reporting, CPS investigation, central registry)
S.D. Codified Laws Chapter 26-7A (Juvenile Court – temporary custody hearings, adjudication, disposition)

regulations_applicable.title: ARSD Article 67:14 - Child Protection Services (Department of Social Services)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed an order directing the county to pay court-appointed counsel in a protection order proceeding, holding SDCL 26-8A-18 authorizes county payment only in proceedings whose particular subject is a child's status or condition as abused or neglected.
key_cases.relevance: This is the South Dakota decision on protection orders in which child abuse is alleged and on who pays for appointed counsel in that proceeding.
key_cases.quote: the circuit court lacked statutory authority in this case to order Minnehaha to pay appointed counsel's costs

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the adjudication and termination, holding that the State proved abuse and neglect by clear and convincing evidence and that DSS need not exhaust every possible form of assistance before termination becomes the least restrictive alternative.
key_cases.relevance: Short-term protective placement at a domestic abuse shelter is treated as a lawful interim protective measure pending adjudication.
key_cases.quote: The State has the burden of proving that the children were abused or neglected by clear and convincing evidence.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed an adjudication of dependency and neglect and a dispositional order temporarily removing custody from the mother, emphasizing that the disposition was not a termination of parental rights but a temporary placement open to periodic review and return.
key_cases.relevance: It frames temporary protective disposition as the less drastic alternative available short of termination.
key_cases.quote: It is a temporary placement subject to periodic review by the court.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed denial of a protection order and of a request to restrict visitation, holding the circuit court was not clearly erroneous in finding that the mother had failed to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the father sexually abused their child.
key_cases.relevance: It is South Dakota's statement of the SDCL 25-10-5 preponderance standard governing a protection order sought on child abuse allegations, and of the clearly-erroneous review that follows.
key_cases.quote: Under SDCL 25-10-5, a circuit court may grant a protection order if it finds by a preponderance of the evidence that abuse has occurred.

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.deadline: 48 hours, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and court holidays
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Child may not be held in temporary custody past 48 hours unless a temporary custody petition has been filed and the court orders longer custody (SDCL 26-7A-14)
